summary: Reviewing the second G1 capture run (every file scanned clean) found values the scan cannot recognise that could link back to an account: ship ids (own and opponents', in battles too), alliance ids, battle ids, item, room, character and other per-account instance ids, and crew names players chose.  - Any field name ending in Id or Ids that is not a user id or a game-data id   (DesignId, SpriteId, TypeId, RaceId, BackgroundId, MissionEventId,   StarSystemId) now gets a stable placeholder per kind (SHIPID-A,   BATTLEID-A...); role-prefixed forms such as AttackingShipId or OwnerShipId   share the kind's labels so cross-references line up, and 0 stays 0. - CharacterName becomes CREW-A... - The server settings summary was withheld because its slash-joined paths   match the long base64 rule. Paths are now dot-joined, and a single name   the scan would flag is shown only by its length.  Regression tests fail on the old module. Re-sanitizing the 30 downloaded captures offline leaves no instance id or crew name and every file clean. Found by reviewing the owner-dispatched G1 capture run; fixed and re-validated by the parent agent.

contract_status_changes.contract: Replace instance ids and crew names in captures; make the settings summary scannable
contract_status_changes.before: Captures keep account-linkable instance ids and crew names; settings summary withheld
contract_status_changes.after: Instance ids and crew names become placeholders; settings summary scans clean
